evals.prompt: I'm building a Next.js app with Create UI. Create a settings form component with fields for: full name, email address, and notification preferences (email, SMS, push notifications as on/off toggles). Add validation states for required fields.
evals.expected_output: A React component using FieldGroup, Field, Switch, data-invalid/aria-invalid validation, gap-* spacing, and Create UI semantic tokens.
expectations: Uses FieldGroup and Field components for form layout instead of a raw div with space-y
Uses Switch for independent on/off notification toggles (not looping Button with manual active state)
Uses data-invalid on Field and aria-invalid on the input control for validation states
Uses gap-* (e.g. gap-4, gap-6) instead of space-y-* or space-x-* for spacing
Uses Create UI semantic tokens (e.g. bg-static, text-body, text-placeholder, text-error-base) - never foreign tokens like bg-background/text-muted-foreground or raw colors like bg-red-500
No manual dark: color overrides (tokens swap via the .dark class)

evals.prompt: Create an account menu component for the app header. The trigger is the user's avatar; the menu shows Profile, Billing, and Settings items with appropriate icons, then a separated Sign out item. Below the menu component, also add a Save changes button that shows a pending state while saving. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: A React component with Dropdown (the trigger is its first non-Popover child: a Button + Avatar with AvatarText initials), a Dropdown.Popover > Dropdown.Menu with Dropdown.Item rows whose icons go through the leading prop, a Dropdown.Separator before Sign out, icons from @create-ui/assets/icons without sizing classes, and a Button using the loading prop.
expectations: Uses Dropdown with the trigger as its first non-Popover child - Dropdown is React Aria Components, not Radix, so there is no DropdownMenuTrigger and no asChild - instead of hand-rolling a menu
Avatar uses AvatarText for the initials fallback (AvatarFallback does not exist in Create UI)
Menu rows are Dropdown.Item inside Dropdown.Menu with a Dropdown.Separator before Sign out; item icons go through the leading prop, never as a child beside the text
Icons are imported from @create-ui/assets/icons (Remix Ri*), never from lucide-react or another icon package
No sizing classes on icons inside components (no size-4, w-4, h-4, etc.) - the component sizes icons via CVA
Uses the Button loading prop for the pending Save state instead of manually composing a Spinner
Button icons (if any) are composed as children alongside <ButtonLabel> (Button takes no leading/trailing props), never via a data-icon attribute

evals.prompt: Create a dashboard stats section that shows 4 stat tiles in a grid. Each tile has a label, a large number, and a percentage-change indicator, plus a loading state while the data is being fetched. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: A React component with stat tiles built from semantic-token markup (bg-static/border-light surfaces, text-placeholder label, text-strongest number), a Badge for the percentage change, a Spinner for the loading state, and gap-* spacing.
expectations: Builds the stat tiles from semantic-token markup (e.g. bg-static or bg-weakest surface, border-light, text-placeholder for the label, text-strongest for the number) - there is no Card component in Create UI
Uses the Spinner component for the loading state instead of a skeleton placeholder (no skeleton component exists in Create UI) or custom animate-pulse/animate-spin divs
Uses a Badge (e.g. variant="success" / "danger") for the percentage change instead of custom styled spans
Uses Create UI semantic tokens (e.g. text-body, text-strongest, text-success-base) instead of foreign tokens or raw colors like bg-green-500
Uses gap-* instead of space-y-* or space-x-* for spacing
Uses size-* when width and height are equal instead of separate w-* h-*

evals.prompt: Create a hero section for a product landing page: an eyebrow badge that says 'Now shipping - v1 components' with a sparkle icon, a large heading, a short description, and two CTA buttons (primary with a trailing arrow icon, secondary ghost). Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: A hero section where the Badge gets its icon via the leading prop, buttons compose icons as children with ButtonLabel, headings/body use semantic text tokens, and the badge does not stretch.
expectations: Badge icon is passed via the leading prop (never as an icon child next to the text, e.g. <Badge><RiSparkling2Line />text</Badge> is wrong)
Button icons are composed as children alongside <ButtonLabel> (Button takes no leading/trailing props)
Icons are imported from @create-ui/assets/icons (Remix Ri*), never lucide-react
No sizing classes on icons inside Badge or Button
Text uses semantic tokens (text-strongest for the heading, text-body/text-placeholder for the description), never raw palette colors
There is no variant="outline"/"secondary"/"destructive" anywhere - outline looks come from appearance="outline"

evals.prompt: Create a settings page section with three tabs: Profile, Billing, and Notifications. Each tab shows its own panel of content. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: Tabs + TabsList + TabsTrigger + TabsContent, with each panel in its own TabsContent paired to its trigger by value; selection via defaultValue (or controlled value/onValueChange).
expectations: Uses the Tabs + TabsList + TabsTrigger + TabsContent set (the content-panel tabs) - never a hand-rolled row of styled buttons; the panels swap in place because each lives in its own TabsContent
Each TabsTrigger value is paired to a TabsContent with the same value - panels are NOT hand-keyed off a useState value (that is the TabMenu pattern, which has no content component)
Tab icons (if any) are passed via the leading prop on TabsTrigger
Selection is driven by defaultValue (or value/onValueChange), not by manual className toggling

evals.prompt: Add a monthly/yearly billing toggle to a pricing section. The active option's background should slide smoothly between the options. Show a '-20%' badge next to the yearly label. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: A SegmentedControl with appearance="grouped" driven by value/onValueChange, plus a Badge for the discount.
expectations: Uses SegmentedControl + SegmentedControlItem with value/onValueChange (or defaultValue) - never a row of Buttons with manual active state
Uses appearance="grouped" for the classic padded pricing-toggle container (the active pill slides in both appearances)
The discount indicator is a Badge, not a custom styled span
An initial value is set (value or defaultValue) so one option is active on mount

evals.prompt: Create a notification preferences panel that feels premium for a marketing showcase: rows for Email, SMS, and Push notifications, each with a label, a description, and a toggle. Make the toggles feel rich, not bare. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: Field/SwitchGroup rows with Switch components that exercise the richer API (thumbIcon, ioTrigger, thumbType, or a deliberate variant), not bare <Switch /> defaults.
expectations: Uses Switch (or SwitchGroup labelled rows - there is no SwitchGroupItem) - never a hand-rolled toggle
At least one richer Switch option is exercised: thumbIcon, ioTrigger, thumbType="long", or a non-default variant - bare <Switch /> everywhere fails the 'premium' ask
Rows are laid out with Field orientation="horizontal" + FieldLabel/FieldDescription (or SwitchGroup), not raw flex divs with hand-styled labels
Switch state is controlled via checked/onCheckedChange or defaultChecked

evals.prompt: Create a marketing site footer: brand column with a short description, three link columns (Product, Resources, Company), a newsletter signup, and a bottom bar with the copyright. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: A footer on neutral semantic surfaces (bg-static/bg-weak, border-light dividers) with TextLink columns, a Field + Input + Button newsletter form, and no raw palette colors.
expectations: Footer surfaces use neutral semantic tokens (bg-static or bg-weak, border-light dividers) - never saturated raw palette colors (bg-blue-500, text-indigo-400) or hex values
Link columns use TextLink (or styled anchors with semantic text tokens like text-body/text-strongest), never primary-colored link soup
Newsletter form is FieldGroup/Field + Input + Button, not raw inputs
Spacing uses flex/grid + gap-*, never space-y-*
Column titles use text-strongest with body links in text-body/text-placeholder

evals.prompt: Build a 'plan limits' summary block: a row that says the account is over its seat limit (an error), a row showing storage is healthy (success), and a neutral row for the current region. Use Create UI semantic tokens.
evals.expected_output: Status communicated with semantic status tokens and/or StatusBadge plus text labels - error family is error-*, neutral is stable-*, no raw palette or danger-* color tokens.
expectations: Error/negative state uses the error-* token family (e.g. text-error-base, bg-error-weak) - never a danger-* color token (there is no danger-* color; danger is only a component variant) and never bg-red-500/hex
Positive state uses success-* tokens (e.g. text-success-base) and informational/neutral uses stable-* or neutral surface tokens - not raw emerald/green/gray palette classes
Status is not conveyed by color alone: each row pairs the color with a text label (or a StatusBadge dot plus an adjacent label)
Surfaces and text use semantic tokens (bg-static/bg-weak, text-body/text-placeholder/text-strongest), never foreign tokens or hex

evals.prompt: Create a checkout details form with: cardholder name, card number, card expiry, a one-time verification code field, the customer's phone number, and their date of birth. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: Each field uses the purpose-built control - CreditCardInput, InputOTP, PhoneInput, DateInput - inside FieldGroup/Field, never a plain Input with hand-rolled masking.
expectations: Card number uses CreditCardInput (not a raw Input with manual formatting)
The verification code uses InputOTP
Phone number uses PhoneInput and date of birth uses DateInput - not plain Inputs
Fields are laid out with FieldGroup + Field (size/state cascade from Field), with FieldLabel wired via htmlFor
No invented or shadcn-style components (no DatePicker, no PhoneNumberInput) - only the registry's actual control names

evals.prompt: Create a billing page with a table of recent invoices (date, amount, status, and a row action menu), an empty state for when there are no invoices, and a 'Cancel subscription' action that asks the user to confirm before proceeding. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: A semantic <table> (no Table primitive) with Badge status cells and a DropdownMenu row action, a semantic empty-state surface, and a confirmation handled inline (expanding section, dedicated step, or InlineAlert) or with a note that Modal is Pro - not an invented Dialog/Card/Table component.
expectations: The table is built from semantic markup (a real <table> with bg-weak header, border-light row separators) - there is no Table/DataTable component; cell content uses primitives (Badge for status, DropdownMenu or an iconOnly Button for the row action) rather than styled spans
No Card primitive is used or imported - surfaces are bg-static/bg-weakest panels with border-light and an elevation shadow

At the free tier there is no Dialog/Modal primitive: the cancel confirmation is surfaced inline (expanding section, dedicated step, or InlineAlert), or the answer notes Modal is Pro - it does not invent a Dialog/AlertDialog component
The empty state reuses the same surface with text-placeholder copy and a primary Button, not a bare 'No data' string or a fixed-height box with only a Spinner
Spacing uses gap-*/padding utilities, not space-y-*, and status colors use semantic tokens

evals.prompt: Create a compact toolbar: an icon-only search button, an icon-only filter button, an icon-only overflow menu, and a view toggle between Grid and List shown as two icons. Make it accessible. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: Icon-only Buttons each with an aria-label, the overflow opening a DropdownMenu, and the view toggle a SegmentedControl with iconOnly items that each carry an aria-label - icons from @create-ui/assets/icons, no sizing classes.
expectations: Every icon-only control has an aria-label (icon-only Buttons and iconOnly SegmentedControlItems) so it has an accessible name
Icon-only buttons set iconOnly and pass the icon as the child (Button has no leading/trailing prop)
The Grid/List toggle is a SegmentedControl with value/onValueChange (or defaultValue), not two manually-toggled Buttons
The overflow menu uses Dropdown with the icon Button as its first non-Popover child (there is no DropdownMenuTrigger / asChild)
Icons come from @create-ui/assets/icons (Ri*), with no size-4/w-4/h-4 sizing classes on icons inside components

evals.prompt: Build a profile photo row for a settings page: the user's avatar on the left, and to its right a 'Profile photo' label with a 'Change' link under it. Make the avatar and the text/link sizes feel balanced and aligned. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: An items-center flex row with an Avatar (AvatarImage + AvatarText) as the visual anchor and a stacked label + TextLink whose sizes track one coherent scale (e.g. Avatar lg with text-body-sm + TextLink size="sm"), spaced with gap-*.
expectations: The row uses flex items-center so the avatar aligns to the optical center of the text block, with a gap-* between them (not margins)
The avatar is the Avatar component with AvatarText for initials (not AvatarFallback) and is the visual anchor of the cluster

The label text token and the TextLink size sit on one coherent scale (e.g. text-body-sm paired with TextLink size="sm"), rather than mismatched sizes - and the answer does not assume Avatar and TextLink share the same size name to align
The change affordance is a TextLink (with a variant/size), not a styled <a> or a Button
Sizes are harmonized by optical height, not by blindly matching size prop names across the Avatar and TextLink

evals.prompt: Create the action bar for an account settings form (a plain app screen, not a marketing page): a 'Save changes' button, a 'Cancel' button, and a 'Delete account' button. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: Buttons whose props reflect their distinct roles - one solid primary Save, a non-solid secondary Cancel, and a danger Delete - not three identical default buttons.
expectations: Save is the single primary action: variant="primary" appearance="solid" - and it is the only solid button in the bar
Cancel is visually secondary (appearance="outline" / "soft" / "ghost"), never a second solid button
Delete account uses variant="danger" (not a default neutral button, and not variant="destructive" which does not exist)
The three buttons are NOT all left at the same default size+variant - their props differ to express primary vs secondary vs destructive roles, even though this is plain app UI rather than a showcase
Sizes are deliberate and consistent for the cluster (not a mix of unrelated sizes), and any icons are composed as children with ButtonLabel (Button has no leading/trailing)

evals.prompt: Build the section navigation for a settings page: a horizontal tab bar with Overview, Members, and Billing that links to /settings, /settings/members, and /settings/billing. The active tab follows the current route. Using Create UI.
evals.expected_output: TabMenu + TabMenuItem with asChild link tabs (each wrapping a next/link or anchor), with the active item driven by the current pathname - not the Tabs content-panel set, since these navigate rather than swap a panel in place.
expectations: Uses TabMenu + TabMenuItem with asChild so each item renders a link (next/link or <a>) - never a hand-rolled row of styled <a>/<button> elements
Does NOT use the Tabs/TabsList/TabsTrigger/TabsContent set: these tabs navigate to routes, there is no in-place content panel to render
The active tab reflects the current route (e.g. selected via pathname), not a local useState toggle
Tab icons (if any) go through leading/trailing on TabMenuItem, never as children next to text
